\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f0\b not
\f1\b0  revise rubric wording, create VOICE-REV change IDs, implement changes, write code, alter architecture, verify live Song / Voice reports, inspect rendered UI behaviour or perform product-release QA.\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 19. Voice / Singing Audit Decision\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-AUDIT complete with explicit limitations; ready for VOICE-REV.
\f1\b0 \
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Rationale\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The current Voice / Singing baseline is fundamentally compatible with VOICE-SYN and the live TapeCoach production architecture. It already contains important strengths: sung vocal is central to Song, acting/storytelling through song is recognised, Step 2 uses locked evidence, material-policy guardrails exist, presentation notes are optional and evidence-grounded, timestamps are locked from Step 1 and normalised chronologically, and deterministic scrubs reduce unsupported visual/source-reference claims.\
The baseline still needs revision because it is under-specified for sung-vocal semantics, vocal-plus-interpretive balance, descriptor specificity, song-framed acting-through-song, musical interpretation visibility, cautious style/subtype handling, accompaniment context, assessability versus merit, anti-polish/resource boundaries, live-room/process-only limits, no-diagnosis vocal-health language, inclusive voice handling, accent/speech-difference fairness, gendered voice assumptions, fixed-material false specificity, generic vocal praise and timestamp/next-take specificity.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Critical blockers\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 No blocker prevents VOICE-REV. All recommended changes are compatible wording, evidence-standard or guardrail changes.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Recommendations to carry into VOICE-REV\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Carry VOICE-AUDIT-R01\'96R18, R20 and R21 into VOICE-REV. Carry VOICE-AUDIT-R19 into Output Specificity / Display Verification planning.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\fs28 \cf0 VOICE-AUDIT handoff summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-AUDIT is complete with explicit limitations and ready for VOICE-REV. The current Voice / Singing baseline is directionally sound but under-specified against VOICE-SYN. It already preserves 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  as Song\'92s central sung-vocal score, recognises acting/storytelling through song as a supporting category, distinguishes technique from lyric storytelling in principle, uses locked Step 1 evidence, blocks Step 2 invention, protects fixed-material policy, keeps presentation optional, grounds presentation notes, preserves timestamps from evidence and sorts timestamped notes chronologically. These strengths must be preserved.\
The audit found twenty issues: sung-vocal field semantics, technique-over-story risk, descriptor specificity, acting-through-song leakage, implicit musical interpretation, style/subtype gaps, belt/mix/registration thinness, assessability versus merit, accompaniment context, live-room overclaim, no-diagnosis vocal-health language, access-safe inclusive voice handling, accent/speech-difference bias, gendered voice/body/voice-type assumptions, repertoire false specificity, external-framework overreach, generic vocal praise, timestamp density, display-layer risk and MT/cross-discipline non-regression.\
VOICE-REV should carry forward recommendations R01\'96R18, R20 and R21. R19 should be carried into output-specificity mapping rather than treated as a baseline wording fix alone. The highest-priority revision themes are: clarify 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  as sung-vocal evidence in Song / MT while preserving Acting and Dance label protections; require vocal-plus-interpretive evidence; expand observable descriptor specificity; keep acting-through-song song-framed; make musical interpretation visible through existing fields; add cautious style/subtype handling; separate audio/technical assessability from vocal merit; block production polish and paid-resource merit; treat accompaniment as context-specific; block live-room/process overclaim; codify no-diagnosis vocal-health language; codify access-safe inclusive voice handling; block accent hierarchy, speech-difference deficit inference, gendered voice assumptions and body/voice-type overclaim; preserve fixed-material policy; suppress generic vocal praise; and strengthen timestamp/next-take specificity.\
No recommendation implies score-field, weighting, schema, backend, pipeline, cap, blocker, verdict, role-fit, server-side recomputation or MT-flow changes. Live Song / Voice outputs were not supplied, so rendered label behaviour, comparison-page parity, timestamp rendering, score stability and live report quality remain pending.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 \strokec2 Audit test map summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-AUDIT-T01\'96T29 cover Song-only label/content containment, acting-scene leakage, MT Vocal visibility, Acting/Dance label non-regression, generic vocal praise, poor audio/track balance, production polish bias, home-recording fairness, fixed-material advice, no-brief invention, short-cut overclaim, belt/mix overclaim, style overreach, accompaniment fairness, paid-resource bias, vocal-health diagnosis, safe strain-like wording, accent/speech-difference bias, hearing/access support, gender-diverse voice stereotyping, live-room/process overclaim, timestamp underproduction, comparison-page mismatch, Step 2 evidence invention and presentation-padding drift.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Baseline compatibility summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 All recommendations are compatible with the live TapeCoach baseline. No score-field, weighting, schema, backend, pipeline, cap, blocker, verdict, role-fit or recomputation change is recommended.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Do-not-change / defer summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Do not change fields, weights, caps, verdicts, role-fit bounds, schema, backend, pipeline, Step 1/Step 2 architecture, locked evidence, deterministic scrubs, material policy or MT acting + song flow. Defer detailed belt, mix, registration, jazz, folk, commercial-pop and actor-musician rubrics.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Generic-feedback and false-specificity summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Block or anchor generic phrases such as \'93strong vocal control\'94, \'93lovely tone\'94, \'93secure pitch\'94, \'93emotional connection\'94, \'93powerful belt\'94, \'93nice mix\'94, \'93strong storytelling\'94, \'93perfect song choice\'94, \'93vocal health sounds good\'94, \'93ready because of voice type\'94 and \'93clean audio as vocal merit\'94. False-specificity risks include invented song titles, universal cut lengths, universal era rules, unsupported role-fit claims, school-specific bans as universal rules and alternative song advice for fixed material.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Safety/accessibility/fairness summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 No vocal-health diagnosis from tape. Strain-like or fatigued sound may be described cautiously but not medicalised. Do not infer respiratory condition, convalescence, psychological state, health status, identity, access need or professional readiness from a finished tape. Treat disability, neurodivergence, hearing access, captions, speech-to-text, sign interpretation, assistive tech, accent, speech difference, gender-diverse voice and reasonable adjustments as access/fairness context, not deficits.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Source-type boundary summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Admissions sources support task/context evidence; formal frameworks support descriptor language only; professional advice supports process and practical phrasing, not universal scoring; union/professional-body sources support fairness and burden; clinical/vocal-health sources support safety boundaries only; accessibility sources support non-deficit guardrails only.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\
**Source-by-Source Evidence Notes**\
\
- **VOICE-S001** says ArtsEd wants a first-round MT song that shows the applicant off, rejects backing tracks, prefers the natural voice over extreme character voicing, and then asks for a second-round pre-1965 legit ballad plus possible vocal exercises and redirection. It can later support legit-style handling, natural-voice language and recall/process boundaries. It cannot support universal song-era rules or a blanket ban on contemporary repertoire. Evidence is both TO and LR; school-specific. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn25view1\u57858 turn25view2\u57858 turn25view3\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S002** says Mountview wants contrasting vocal approaches, one more classical-sounding in MT, correct key, songs that let the applicant act through them, and no opera/classical repertoire for the MT routes. It can support acting-through-song wording and legit/contemporary contrast. It cannot support Mountview\'92s exact genre exclusions as universal scoring. Mostly TO, with workshops/redirection on recall. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn32view0\u57858 turn32view1\u57858 turn32view2\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S003** says RAM wants three songs that show different voice qualities, a separate vocal-range demonstration, continuous unedited files, simple acoustics and balanced audio, and songs that still show the full journey even when cut. It can support visible range/voice-quality evidence and assessability guidance. It cannot support camera-readiness or self-tape polish as talent evidence. Both TO and process. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn31view0\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S004** says GSA distinguishes legit pre-1965 from contemporary post-1965 in MT routes and also separates actor-musician requirements. It can support era/style contrast and actor-musician boundaries. It cannot support any claim that all song assessments must be pre-/post-1965. Both TO and LR; school-specific but recurring. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn33view0\u57858 turn33view1\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S005** says RWCMD foregrounds technical and expressive ability in voice, movement and singing, plus plain background, clear audio, one-take components and accommodations for disability or recording circumstances. It can support assessability and fair-context handling. It cannot support song-subtype rules because the page is descriptor-light on repertoire. Both TO and process. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn24view1\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S006** says RCS BA MT asks for two contrasting songs, at least one MT, songs that show vocal range, and permits a cappella if accompaniment is not possible. It adds a devised recall piece and instrument pathway context. It can support contrast, range evidence and actor-musician adjacency. It cannot support recall creativity as tape evidence. Both TO and LR. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn27view0\u57858 turn27view1\u57858 turn27view2\u57858 turn27view3\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S007** says RCS classical voice expects three contrasting classical pieces, language variation, memory and possible aural tasks. It can support a classical art-song / opera-adjacent subtype boundary. It cannot support importing classical voice requirements into MT/song scoring. Both TO and LR. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn9view2\u57858 turn9view3\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S008** says RCS Music recorded guidelines require a continuous shot, visible body/instrument, and explicitly state that lack of accompaniment should not disadvantage the applicant. It can later support assessability and low-resource fairness language. It cannot support voice-quality scoring. Process-only. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn9view4\u57858 turn9view5\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S009** says USC wants two contrasting MT cuts, not to \'93impress\'94 with range, and instead asks for material that fits the voice, carries an emotional arc and clear objective, with acceptable digital tracks and no need for professional filming. It can strongly support story-over-display language and anti-polish boundaries. It cannot support USC\'92s exact prescreen format as universal. Both TO and LR. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn11view0\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S010** says NYU wants one theatre-canon cut and one contrasting cut, may test range, and explicitly frames the singing work around age-appropriate material, addressee, objective and engagement through the music. It can support lyric intention and acting-through-song evidence. It cannot support a universal requirement for live audition structure. Both TO and LR. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn12view0\u57858 turn12view1\u57858 turn12view2\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S011** says NYU\'92s digital singing instructions are precise about framing, eye level, piano rather than karaoke, and voice-over-track balance. It can support self-tape assessability and the need to separate audio balance from vocal merit. It cannot support judging a singer by equipment sophistication. TO for assessability; otherwise process. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn12view3\u57858 turn12view4\u57858 turn12view5\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S012** says Carnegie Mellon Voice is a classical-voice route, not MT, and expects language variation, memory, a cappella scale/arpeggio and stylistic range, while excluding MT, jazz and CCM. It can support a strong classical-voice boundary. It cannot support excluding those genres from general TapeCoach song assessment. TO + LR; specialist route. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn13search0\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S013** says the MT Common Prescreen formalises contrasting songs, broad style families, balanced sound, standard devices, waist-up framing, and gives examples such as belt vs head/falsetto mix. It can support recurring cross-school source patterns. It cannot support treating any option set as universal scoring or school-specific. Mostly TO and process-framework. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn26view0\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S014** says Oklahoma explicitly asks applicants to think about contrast in style, composer and legit/belt, and if using commercial music to produce an authentic non-theatre sound. It can support style-authenticity evidence and legit/belt distinction. It cannot support rewarding \'93commercial sound\'94 universally outside source-supported context. Both TO and LR. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn15search0\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S015** says National Youth Choir accepts any genre, unaccompanied and from memory, with vocal exercises and musicianship tasks that assess readiness to learn and potential rather than only current polish. It can support unaccompanied singing and potential/process limits. It cannot support choir musicianship tasks as universal tape scoring. Both TO and LR. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn30view0\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S016** says BYMT auditions are group workshops with no pre-prepared song, learning a new song on the day, group movement, teamwork, retention and perseverance, with explicit emphasis on authenticity, tenacity and generosity. It can support strong process-only boundaries. It cannot support scoring those capacities from a finished self-tape unless directly shown. LR/process-only almost entirely. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn29view0\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S017** says RCS Juniors wants a MT song that tells a story, uses piano, fits the right key, and may be redirected at audition. It can support story-led song evidence, key/accompanist handling and direction-response boundaries. It cannot support youth-training expectations as identical to adult audition scoring. Both TO and LR. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn28view0\u57858 turn28view1\u57858 turn28view2\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S018** says GSA Actor-Musician allows a musical theatre song or jazz standard with backing track or self-accompaniment, plus a separate first instrument piece. It can support actor-musician and self-accompaniment subtypes. It cannot support collapsing instrumental evidence into general song scoring. Both TO and LR. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn20search0\u57858 turn20search1\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S019** says Chapman asks for one or two songs in one video, no fixed style split, encourages demonstration of vocal range, and requires live or recorded accompaniment with balanced sound. It can support balance/range basics. It cannot support saying style never matters; the source is a minor-programme audition page rather than a specialised BFA MT admissions rubric. TO with a programme-scope limitation. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn22view0\u57857 \
- **VOICE-S020** says Nazareth follows MTCP for prescreening but asks, at live audition, for two contrasting songs showing singing in tune, good quality and musical intelligence, with at least one MT and one pop/contemporary song. It can support explicit tune/quality/intelligence language and MT/pop split. It cannot support those terms without later descriptor work, and it cannot turn fee-waiver process into scoring logic. Both TO and LR. \uc0\u57856 cite\u57858 turn23view0\u57858 turn23view2\u57858 turn23view3\u57857 \

## Handoff for VOICE-B2\
\
**Reusable Handoff Pack for VOICE-B2**\
\
VOICE-B1 extracted all 20 assigned official / quasi-official source rows and closed every row with a final status. Seventeen rows are official admissions or programme pages from UK and US conservatoires, drama schools, universities, youth choirs or youth MT providers; one row is an official cross-institution framework source (MT Common Prescreen / Acceptd); one row is an official process-only recorded-audition guidance page; and one row is a minor-programme audition page with limited subtype detail. No source row remains unresolved.\
\
The clearest B1 pattern is that contrast is real but not uniform. Official sources repeatedly ask for contrasting songs, but the contrast varies by institution: pre-/post-1965, pre-/post-1970, legit vs contemporary, canon vs contemporary, different voice qualities, or MT plus another genre. This supports a true style/subtype map for Voice / Singing, but not a single universal admissions rule. The strongest recurring subtype anchors are classical/legit, contemporary MT, classical voice / art song, actor-musician, pop-commercial crossover, jazz-standard context, and unaccompanied song.\
\
The second major pattern is that song assessment is not just technique display. Multiple official sources explicitly ask candidates to act through songs, tell a story, show emotional arc, clarify objective/addressee, or reveal musical intelligence. This is the strongest B1 support for keeping acting/storytelling visible inside Song without turning song reports into acting-scene reports.\
\
The third major pattern is assessability-first capture guidance. RAM, RWCMD, RCS, USC, NYU, MTCP and Chapman all stress clear sound, balanced accompaniment, eye-level framing, simple or low-cost setups, and acceptable phone capture. Several sources explicitly reduce production-polish pressure. This is strong evidence that audio and technical clarity are preconditions for fair singing assessment, not vocal merit in themselves.\
\
B1 also sharply clarifies live-room boundaries. Recalls, redirection, learning a new song, workshop collaboration, interviews, musicianship tasks and training-potential judgments are repeatedly located in live or process contexts rather than in submitted song tape alone. This should later feed claim-scope rules and output-specificity tests.\
\
Main deferred gaps for VOICE-B2 are descriptor language: pitch, tone, phrasing, diction, breath/support, musical interpretation, registration, and more detailed belt/mix/pop-rock/jazz/folk language. VOICE-B4 must later handle vocal-health safety, accessibility, speech difference, neurodivergence and gender-diverse voice considerations. Exact source IDs used in B1: VOICE-S001\'96VOICE-S020. Relevant provisional findings: VOICE-B1-F01\'96F05.\
\
**Recommended focus for VOICE-B2 Formal Frameworks / Descriptor Extraction**\
\
- Formal descriptor sources for pitch, rhythm, tone, phrasing, diction, musical communication and performance interpretation.\
- Carefully bounded legit / belt / mix / classical / CCM terminology.\
- Descriptor vocabulary that can improve report specificity without importing external grades, marks or weights.\
- Continued separation of tape-observable evidence from process-only musicianship, coaching or health claims.\
\

**Source-by-Source Evidence Notes**

**VOICE-S021 — LAMDA Exams Musical Theatre**  
The official LAMDA Musical Theatre Solo/Duo syllabus is criterion-referenced and repeatedly couples interpretation with technique. Across grades it names audibility, fluency, focus, clear diction, accurate melody and rhythm, sustained vocal control, and—at higher levels—appropriate breathing, voice production and resonance. It also expects understanding of character, mood, place/period, and response to the vocal demands of characterisation, plus question-based knowledge tasks. Reasonable adjustments are explicitly built into the qualification framework. This source can later support observable wording for clarity, control, melody/rhythm, diction, resonance-like description and acting-through-song, but it cannot support importing LAMDA marks, grade bands, knowledge-question structures or spoken-song exam design into TapeCoach. Evidence is mixed: much is tape-observable, while knowledge answers and some grade-specific tasks are process/exam-only. citeturn16view0turn26view0turn27view2turn27view4turn27view5

**VOICE-S022 — LAMDA Exams Singing**  
Within the official LAMDA exam families accessed in this run, the public syllabus/download-centre material showed Introductory, Performance, Communication, Musical Theatre, Group, PCertLAM and Shakespeare families, but no standalone Singing qualification row. This row therefore cannot support Voice/Singing descriptor extraction and is closed as out of scope rather than left unresolved. citeturn16view0

**VOICE-S023 — Trinity College London Musical Theatre**  
The official Trinity Musical Theatre syllabus provides unusually direct acting-through-song language. Candidates are expected to sing and move in time with the music, perform audibly, clearly and accurately, vary pace, pitch and volume to create character and support narrative, use movement/dance and space to support character and narrative, communicate understanding of the material and connection with character, make choices of interpretation, and communicate meaning and mood with audience awareness. It also exists explicitly in face-to-face and digital formats. This can later support integrated MT descriptors and claim-scope rules, but it cannot justify importing Trinity’s movement expectations or qualification structure into Song-only casting-tape scoring. Evidence is mixed: core performance language is observable, while reflection/supporting-task elements are formal-framework/process-only. citeturn18view1turn18view3turn18view4

**VOICE-S024 — Trinity College London Singing**  
The official Trinity Singing overview confirms a current 2023 syllabus approach with digital and face-to-face delivery, broad style/genre range, separate high/low voice books without gender restriction, a dedicated sight-reading format for singers, and strong Musical Theatre presence inside the broader singing route. Official digital-recording guidance requires a quiet space, whole body and face in view, enough facial visibility to assess focus and personal investment, one continuous take, and allows recorded accompaniments in digital exams. The public page also points to healthy vocal technique as a teaching/publication theme. This source can later support wide style-range language, assessability-first framing and digital capture conditions, but the direct public syllabus fetch was throttled, so fine-grained singing descriptors remain partial. It cannot support importing Trinity’s product/book architecture or digital-exam rules wholesale into TapeCoach scoring. Evidence is mixed and partly dispersed. citeturn34view1turn34view2turn34view4turn35view1turn35view2turn36view3turn37view1

**VOICE-S025 — ABRSM Singing**  
The official ABRSM Singing qualification specification and official marking criteria converge on a stable descriptor family: pitch, time, tone, shape and performance. The marking criteria then unpack these into notes/intonation, tempo/rhythmic character, well projected or controlled tonal qualities, expressive musical shaping/detail, and communication of character and style. The singing specification also keeps songs flexible as to key and language/translation, and includes access arrangements for candidates with specific needs. This source can later support precise non-generic language for pitch/intonation, tempo/rhythm, tone/tonal awareness, shape/phrasing and performance communication, especially in classical/legit and formal singing contexts. It cannot support importing ABRSM marks, distinctions/merits, full exam structure, or sight-singing/aural tasks as equivalent to a finished song self-tape. Evidence is mixed between tape-observable performance and formal supporting tests. citeturn28view1turn28view3turn30view4turn31view0turn31view2turn31view3turn31view6turn32view1turn32view3

**VOICE-S026 — ABRSM Singing for Musical Theatre**  
The official ABRSM Singing for Musical Theatre practical syllabus is one of the strongest formal MT vocal sources in this batch. It explicitly frames the route around three accompanied songs and one unaccompanied song, communication of character and style, relevant sight-singing for MT singers, aural tests, and fair access arrangements. The official marking criteria add notes/intonation, rhythm, tonal qualities, musical shaping/detail and vivid story-telling. The performance-grade route adds whole-programme musical intent, communication, interpretation, delivery and even stamina/control across transitions. This source can later support acting-through-song, unaccompanied singing, musical communication, interpretation and careful use of “story-telling” language. It cannot support importing ABRSM route design, marks, or supporting-test expectations as direct Song-tape scoring logic. Evidence is mixed between tape-observable performance and formal exam components. citeturn28view0turn28view2turn28view3turn29view3turn29view4turn29view5turn29view8turn32view1

**VOICE-S027 — LCME Musical Theatre**  
The official LCME *Musical Theatre for Singers* syllabus supplies unusually explicit assessment-domain wording. Its assessment objectives are technical accomplishment, interpretation, knowledge and understanding, and communication. It names audibility, clarity of diction, fluency, projection, intonation, sense of spontaneity, character portrayal, movement and gesture, use of space, facial expression, accent, breath control, and variety as part of technical accomplishment, while higher grades require seamless integration of vocal and dramatic skills and thoughtful interpretation of musical and textual syntax to convey subtleties of meaning. The official digital-recording guidance then adds quiet room, static camera, single microphone, sufficient quality for tone quality and dynamic range, candidate continuously in shot, balanced backing track, and one continuous unedited file. This can later support rich observable MT-for-singers language and assessability rules. It cannot support importing LCME percentages, discussion/written-programme requirements, or assuming all singing assessment includes movement/space. Evidence is strongly mixed across tape-observable performance and process-only discussion/knowledge components. citeturn18view7turn18view8turn18view9turn38view0turn38view3turn38view5turn39view3

**VOICE-S028 — LCME Singing**  
The official LCME Classical Singing page confirms a formal classical route with technical work, performance, discussion, sight reading and aural tests, while the currently linked public syllabus for Classical Singing resolves through the broader *Music Grades* specification. That broader framework supports classical/formal route boundaries, discussion-based musicianship, stylistic range and formal assessment architecture, but it gives thinner singing-specific descriptor detail than the MT-for-singers syllabus. This row can therefore support classical/art-song context and formal-framework task boundaries, but it cannot carry a rich singing-only descriptor family on its own and should be treated as partial evidence. It also cannot justify importing general LCME grade bands or percentages into TapeCoach. citeturn20view1turn21view0turn21view1turn21view2turn22view0

**VOICE-S029 — RSL / Rockschool Vocals**  
The official Rockschool/RSL Vocals course page was sufficient to close the row because it states both exam structure and assessment criteria. For performance pieces it names clear production of sound and even tone quality, synchronisation to music or internal pulse, accuracy and understanding of musical structure, and convincing projection/style-expression. The same official page also keeps unseen tests, ear tests and general musicianship questions as separate formal components, including improvisation and interpretation or quick-study work at different levels. This source can later support contemporary/pop-friendly wording for pulse, tone evenness, projection, structural understanding and interpretation. It cannot support importing RSL marks or course architecture, and it does not provide strong explicit belt/mix language in the accessed official source. ## Handoff for B3

**Reusable Handoff Pack for VOICE-B3**

VOICE-B2 reviewed formal framework sources from official pages and linked specifications across entity["organization","LAMDA","uk drama exams"], entity["organization","Trinity College London","music exams uk"], entity["organization","ABRSM","royal schools music board"], entity["organization","London College of Music Examinations","uwl exams uk"] and entity["organization","RSL Awards","rockschool exams uk"]. The strongest outcome is a stable formal descriptor spine for Voice / Singing: formal frameworks repeatedly pair observable vocal control language with observable communication/interpretation language. Across the strongest sources, B2 now supports precise vocabulary for pitch and intonation, rhythm/tempo/pulse, tonal control/evenness, musical shape/phrasing, audibility and diction, plus communication of character and style, story-telling, interpretation, audience engagement and acting-through-song. The strongest fully extracted rows are S021 LAMDA Musical Theatre, S023 Trinity Musical Theatre, S025 ABRSM Singing, S026 ABRSM Singing for Musical Theatre, S027 LCME Musical Theatre, and S029 RSL Vocals. S024 Trinity Singing and S028 LCME Singing are useful but remain partial because the public evidence was thinner or technically limited. S022, S030 and S031 are closed with explicit non-positive statuses, not left unresolved.

B2 also sharpened the boundary between tape-observable evidence and formal/process-only evidence. Sight-singing, aural tests, discussion, reflection, general musicianship questions, some knowledge work and some whole-programme stamina claims belong primarily to formal exam contexts and should not later be overclaimed from a finished song tape. Digital guidance from Trinity and LCME additionally strengthens the assessability-first position: quiet room, usable audio, visible face/body, balanced accompaniment and one continuous take are conditions for fair assessment, not artistic merit.

Style/subtype coverage improved but remains uneven. B2 now supports real distinctions for classical/legit, contemporary Musical Theatre, classical art song, contemporary/pop vocal contexts, accompanied vs unaccompanied work, and MT-integrated storytelling. It does **not** yet supply robust formal descriptor support for belt, mix, detailed registration language, or a rich jazz/folk/commercial descriptor family. Accessibility is also still broad: access arrangements and reasonable adjustments appear, but speech difference, inclusive voice practice, gender-diverse voice considerations and health-safety boundaries remain mainly B4 work.

Recommended focus for VOICE-B3 is therefore professional and casting-process evidence: self-tape and recorded-audio practice, singer audition guidance, accompaniment/backing-track handling, song self-tape framing, wording that separates assessability from polish, and claim-scope limits around audition-room direction, stamina, learning speed and rehearsal/callback behaviours. Exact source IDs used in B2: VOICE-S021, VOICE-S022, VOICE-S023, VOICE-S024, VOICE-S025, VOICE-S026, VOICE-S027, VOICE-S028, VOICE-S029, VOICE-S030, VOICE-S031.

**Source-by-Source Evidence Notes**

- **VOICE-S032**: Spotlight explicitly supports smartphone filming, eye-level setup, mid-close framing, tight eyeline, quieter readers, simple/plain backgrounds, background-noise control, file naming, format conversion and restrained versioning. It can later support assessability, framing, ident/slate handling and submission hygiene. It cannot support singer-specific accompaniment, style or lyric interpretation. Evidence is mostly tape-observable/process-mixed, broadly recurring across self-tape practice, and status is fully extracted. citeturn18view2turn18view4turn35view0turn31search0

- **VOICE-S033**: Equity explicitly treats simplicity as best practice, discourages set-building at home, sets limits around turnaround and first-tape burden, says readers help but must not be compulsory or performer-funded, and adds access guidance on formats, extra time and support needs. It can later support fair-process, burden, access and claim-scope rules. It cannot support vocal technique or song-style scoring. Evidence is professional-process and access-focused, broadly recurrent in fair-audition guidance, and status is fully extracted. Commercials-specific “judge performance, not equipment” language must not be universalised without caution. citeturn19view1turn19view4turn19view0turn17search6

- **VOICE-S034**: SAG-AFTRA’s accessible material supports technical/text/transfer as core self-tape pillars, says performers do not need major kit, emphasises lighting/audio simplicity, keep props minimal, file transfer usability and naming, and includes provenance-limited official snippet evidence that live virtual alternatives may be requested in some contexts. It can support general self-tape burden/process boundaries. It cannot support singer-specific accompaniment, interpretation or formal song criteria. Evidence is official but only partly singer-relevant and partly snippet-limited; no marks/grades apply; status is partial with explicit limitation. citeturn16view0turn15search0turn15search1turn0search2

- **VOICE-S035**: Backstage explicitly supports medium close framing, eye-level camera, audible but non-distracting reader, slate only when asked, and audio clarity as a condition that keeps focus on performance rather than as talent evidence. Its MT song guidance supports 16/32-bar cuts, classic/contemporary MT, pop-rock/country, Disney light mix, jazz/blues and folk/other categories, and says songs should show acting skills as well as range and fit the show style/voice type. It can later support style-map and acting-through-song phrasing, but it must not be treated as universal scoring because it is practitioner-shaped. citeturn33view4turn20view0turn28view4turn28view2

- **VOICE-S036**: Playbill explicitly treats self-tapes as equivalent to walking into the room, warns against turning them into a “music video or a short film”, supports smartphone capture with a proper tripod, neutral backdrops and non-overproduced lighting, and links singing-specific mic distance to prevent audio distortion in louder material. The singing-audition page supports diction clarity, open-eyed communication, addressee, lyric speaking for emotional levels, hope and freshness of moment. It can later support interpretive song language and anti-overproduction boundaries. It cannot support universal repertoire rules, belt/mix criteria or fixed scoring because it is practitioner/interview-shaped. citeturn34view4turn21view1turn21view3turn21view6

- **VOICE-S037**: The usable current The Stage evidence is stronger on limits than on technique. One accessible opinion piece argues self-tapes are a starting point rather than the whole process and calls sole reliance on them limiting and discriminatory; the self-tape advice result also supports plain-background/process basics. It can later support live-room claim-scope restraint and anti-self-tape-overclaim. It cannot support robust singing criteria, and the evidence is partly paywall/opinion-limited. Status is partial with explicit limitation. citeturn22view5turn10search2turn36view0

- **VOICE-S038**: The current MT Common Prescreen page clearly covers waist-up framing, separate media, eye-level camera, balanced pre-recorded accompaniment, standard devices and a single short slate. However, this source family was already extracted in B1; it therefore remains a duplicate/alias and is not double-counted here. It can support later process recall through B1, but adds no distinct B3 source-family coverage. citeturn23view2turn23view1

- **VOICE-S039**: Disney On Broadway explicitly asks for style-specific 16-bar video submissions, with sheet music, via YouTube/Vimeo links rather than file attachments. Lion King asks for R&B/pop/rock material; Aladdin asks for an uptempo MT song; both ban show material. The page also makes callback contact conditional. It can later support fixed-material boundaries, style-specific choice handling and process-only callback claims. It cannot support general scoring rules because the asks are production-specific. Status is fully extracted. citeturn38view0

- **VOICE-S040**: The Muny’s current official pages and linked self-tape guidance provide unusually strong process evidence: 16- or 32-bar prep depending on call, contrasting selection if requested, accompanist provided in live calls, official callback scheduling, and explicit self-tape guidance that recording quality itself is not the basis of evaluation because performers have different resources. It also specifies medium full framing for singing, eye-level camera, soft-room acoustics, clarity, reduced echo, side-of-lens eyeline, short slate and a three-take limit to preserve spontaneity. It can later support assessability-first, anti-polish, authenticity and live-room boundary language. Company-specific wardrobe/YouTube preferences must not become scoring rules. citeturn30search0turn29search2turn26view0

- **VOICE-S041**: OPERA America’s official guidance is the strongest singer-specific process source in B3. It explicitly says singing quality is not linked to access to technology, that lack of a live pianist must not count against singers, and that companies should state whether they accept video/audio, current/recent recordings, a cappella work, self-accompaniment, split-screen, editing and headphone use. For singers it covers room acoustics, clear audio over reverberant spaces, acceptable single-source recording, use the best available phone/laptop/mic, fixed horizontal camera, upper-body framing, unusual but workable rooms, accessible upload settings and the continued distinction between recorded and live audition experience. It can strongly support assessability, accompaniment, low-resource fairness and claim-scope limits, but remains opera-specific and partly 2020 remote-context shaped. citeturn27view0turn27view1turn27view3turn27view5

- **VOICE-S042**: No exact additional VOICE-S0 professional-process row was supplied in the current run, and none was invented. It therefore supports only a source-absence limitation, not evidence extraction. Status is not found.

**B4 Decision**

**VOICE-B4 appears required.**

B3 materially improved the professional/process spine, especially around self-tape assessability, anti-polish boundaries, accompaniment handling and live-room claim-scope. It did **not** close the major safety/fairness gaps that were already flagged at preflight and after B2: vocal-health diagnosis boundaries remain under-evidenced; accessibility is still broad rather than operational; speech difference, hearing difference, neurodivergence, gender-diverse voice considerations, inclusive voice practice, backing-track/accompanist inequality and recording-equipment inequality still need dedicated extraction; and body/appearance/age/voice-assumption guardrails still need stronger source support than B3 provides. citeturn19view0turn17search19turn27view0turn27view5

Those gaps are not just optional refinements. They affect whether later synthesis can produce safe, fair, non-deficit Voice / Singing language. Some minor thin areas, such as jazz/folk depth or detailed belt terminology, can be carried as synthesis limitations, but the accessibility/fairness/vocal-health boundary set is important enough that it should be addressed before VOICE-SYN. The B4 source-family plan was already available from preflight and S0.

## Reusable handoff and completion

**Reusable Handoff Pack for VOICE-B4 or VOICE-SYN**

VOICE-B3 extracted 11 assigned source rows across official performer-platform guidance, union fair-process guidance, professional/practitioner advice, official company casting pages, an official theatre open-call set and one singer-specific professional organisation source. The clearest B3 result is a strong assessability-first professional process spine. Across Spotlight, Equity, SAG-AFTRA, Backstage, Playbill, The Muny and OPERA America, self-tape song work is repeatedly framed as needing readable sound, stable framing, sensible eyeline, workable acoustics, balanced accompaniment and straightforward submission handling. Just as importantly, several sources explicitly push against overproduction: simplicity matters, home tools are acceptable, artistry is not technology, and performers should not be judged on expensive equipment or elaborate setups. This is the strongest new support for keeping audio/technical comments clearly separate from vocal merit. citeturn18view2turn19view1turn16view0turn26view0turn27view0

B3 also confirms that professional song audition expectation is not technique-only display. Backstage, Playbill and The Muny all give practical support for lyric/storytelling language: acting skills as well as range, addressee, diction clarity, speaking lyrics for emotional levels, authenticity, energy, listening and connection. This strengthens the case for keeping acting/storytelling visible within Song while continuing to block pure acting-scene leakage. Official open-call pages then add real process boundaries: Disney and The Muny show that song-length asks, style restrictions, show-material bans, provided accompaniment or live callbacks are contextual instructions, not universal standards. OPERA America gives the strongest singer-specific process guidance in the batch, especially on acoustics, accompaniment options, technology inequality and the fact that recorded auditions do not replace the live experience. citeturn28view0turn21view3turn38view0turn30search0turn27view1turn24view1

Compact source-status summary: fully extracted rows were S032, S033, S035, S036, S039, S040 and S041; partial rows were S034 and S037; S038 closed as duplicate/alias; S042 closed as not found. Provisional findings are VOICE-B3-F01 assessability-first and anti-polish boundaries; VOICE-B3-F02 songs as vocal-plus-interpretive storytelling evidence; and VOICE-B3-F03 live-room/process boundaries for callbacks, redirection, stamina and wider readiness.

Risk summary: B3 reduces technique-over-story, production-polish-as-merit and live-room-overclaim risk strongly or partially, but does little to resolve vocal-health diagnosis risk, speech-difference/accessibility risk, or the broader inclusive voice-practice gap. Style/subtype process coverage improved for contemporary MT, pop-rock, jazz/folk mentions, classical/opera, a cappella/self-accompanied handling and open-call cut structure, but detailed belt/mix/registration language remains thin.

Baseline preservation notes: nothing in B3 implies changes to score fields, weights, schema, pipeline, caps, verdicts, role-fit bounds or MT acting+song stability. All source-specific rules remain contextual and must not become universal scoring.

Source limitations and deferred issues: S034 relies partly on snippet-level official evidence; S037 is opinion/paywall-limited; S041 is opera-specific and partly 2020 remote-context shaped; S042 was not supplied. Output label/display behaviour, live Song/Voice outputs, score stability and timestamp rendering remain untested.

**B4 decision:** **VOICE-B4 appears required.**  
**Recommended focus for VOICE-B4:** accessibility, fairness, vocal-health-safety and inclusive voice practice only; especially speech difference, accent/dialect bias, hearing difference, neurodivergence, disability/access support, gender-diverse voice considerations where source-supported, diagnosis boundaries, backing-track/accompanist inequality, recording-equipment inequality, body/appearance assumptions and age/voice-maturity assumptions.  
**Exact source IDs used:** VOICE-S032, VOICE-S033, VOICE-S034, VOICE-S035, VOICE-S036, VOICE-S037, VOICE-S038, VOICE-S039, VOICE-S040, VOICE-S041, VOICE-S042.

**VOICE-B4 appears required. Next prompt should run VOICE-B4 accessibility, fairness, vocal-health-safety and inclusive voice extraction only.**

## Source-by-source evidence notes

### VOICE-S043 evidence note

British Voice Association evidence supports a practical, non-diagnostic voice-care boundary. Its public leaflets advise hydration, warm-up, rest, humidification, avoiding shouting or whispering through symptoms, and seeking medical advice if the voice remains changed for more than two weeks. The online-voice leaflet additionally shows that technology, headphones, microphones, breaks and room setup affect vocal load rather than artistic merit. The ageing and children’s-voice pages add two important fairness points: age-related change varies widely by person, and during adolescence healthy voices can sometimes sound unstable or “unhealthy”, so age or maturity should not be overread from a recording. This row can later support safety guardrails and age/voice-maturity cautions. It cannot support diagnosis, hormone inference, mental-state inference or any new scoring category. The evidence is mixed: partly tape-observable at the level of cautious description, but largely safety-only and contextual. It is broadly recurring and not merely one-school taste. citeturn5view1turn5view2turn17view0turn22view0

### VOICE-S044 evidence note

The equivalent S044 source, resolved to BAPAM, gives the clearest performer-specific safety language in the batch. It defines vocal overload in terms of prolonged use, loud use, shouting, screaming or extremes of range, and describes signs such as hoarseness, discomfort, reduced range and fatigue-like strain. It also connects overload risk to room acoustics, monitoring, amplification, dehydration, infection and rehearsal structure. Crucially, BAPAM says voice changes or throat discomfort lasting more than two weeks should trigger professional assessment and that specialist examination is needed to decide treatment. This can later support hard no-diagnosis rules and cautious wording about strain-like sound. It cannot support pathology labelling, treatment advice, or importing rehearsal/workload recommendations as scoring rules. The evidence is strongly safety-only and process-only, though some sign language is cautiously observable. citeturn21view0turn21view1turn7view1

### VOICE-S045 evidence note

The NHS and ENT UK pages provide a clean clinical boundary: hoarseness, lost voice and sore throat may look similar from the outside, but persistent or recurring symptoms need medical review rather than lay diagnosis. They also reiterate that loud talking, whispering, smoke, dust and dehydration can worsen symptoms. This row can support the claim that a finished tape must not be used to infer laryngitis, pathology, respiratory condition or similar diagnoses. It cannot support singing-rubric language beyond safety caution, and it adds no audition-specific access guidance. The evidence is clinical-information-only. citeturn8view1turn8view2

### VOICE-S046 evidence note

Musicians’ Union evidence is especially valuable because it pairs performer-health information with equality rights. On health, the MU directs singers towards specialist clinic assessment and repeats that nobody can know the correct treatment without viewing the vocal folds. On disability and neurodivergence, the MU frames reasonable adjustments as proactive fairness measures, says equality is about fair outcomes rather than identical treatment, and describes neurodiversity as natural human variation rather than deficit. It also points to hearing-health support and adaptive-instrument funding/access routes. This row can later support guardrails around reasonable adjustments, disabled and neurodivergent musician handling, and no-diagnosis principles. It cannot justify using legal thresholds, union benefits or educational methods as score logic. The evidence is mainly access/process and safety context, not tape-derived merit evidence. citeturn9view0turn9view2turn25view0turn25view1turn23view0

### VOICE-S047 evidence note

RNID evidence is the strongest hearing-access source in the batch. It covers captions, sign interpretation, hearing loops, streamers, assistive listening devices, speech-to-text tools, video-conferencing accessibility features and the fact that regulated communication support is preferable in formal settings. It also shows that listening duration and volume matter for hearing safety, and that many accessibility tools carry real costs. This row can later support hearing-difference guardrails, captioning and tech-access fairness, and the principle that hearability and communication access are not proxies for talent. It cannot support vocal scoring, nor can it justify treating assistive tech or captions as professionalism deficits. The evidence is access-only and hearing-safety-only. citeturn11view1turn11view2turn26view0turn26view1

### VOICE-S048 evidence note

Drake Music provides some of the most useful inclusive-process evidence in the whole B4 batch. Its application-access page explicitly argues that telling applicants merely to email for adjustments creates extra “disability admin”, consumes time and energy, and can deter applicants because of fear of refusal. It therefore supports proactive access support and alternative formats rather than putting extra burden on disabled applicants. Its technology and training pages frame accessible instruments, disability equality and mixed-format participation as barrier removal, not remediation of personal deficit. This row can later support inclusive application and submission guardrails, especially around not penalising people for how they need to access a process. It cannot support any direct singing-score criteria. The evidence is access/process-only and broadly recurring in inclusion practice. citeturn12view1turn12view2turn12view3

### VOICE-S049 evidence note

The Johns Hopkins page is high-authority evidence that gender-diverse voice work should be identity-led rather than stereotype-led. It explains that some people want more neutral or nonbinary outcomes rather than stereotypically masculine or feminine ones, and that vocal parameters such as pitch, resonance, articulation and nonverbal cues are options around identity and preference. It also notes that long-term self-modulation can leave a voice strained, weak or raspy, which reinforces the need for caution and support rather than judgement. This row can later support gender-diverse voice guardrails and anti-stereotype handling. It cannot support gendered role-fit assumptions, therapy-pathway judgements or medicalised inferences from tape. The evidence is clinical/support-only. citeturn13view1

### VOICE-S050 evidence note

Accent Bias Britain gives the strongest evidence in the batch against accent hierarchy. It states that all speakers have an accent, that “standard” accents are prestigious because of power rather than intrinsic quality, and that asking candidates to adopt a prestige accent is unrealistic and unfair. Its intervention findings also show that awareness can reduce accent-based differences in competence ratings and that decisions should focus on objective criteria, knowledge and skills rather than accent. This row can later support anti-bias guardrails for diction and intelligibility handling. It cannot support positive scoring descriptors for speech difference, and it remains accent-focused rather than covering the full speech-difference universe. The evidence is hiring-context and policy-context rather than tape-derived performance evidence. citeturn14view0turn14view1

### VOICE-S051 evidence note

VOICE-S051 remained partial, but still added useful access-equity evidence. The Digital Lifeline evaluation shows that devices, data, assistive technology, digital skills and support networks materially affect whether disabled people can participate online at all. The Take It Away guide and MU coverage show parallel equipment and funding barriers for disabled musicians through adaptive instruments and accessible technology. This row can later support the principle that access to devices, connectivity, assistive tech and specialist equipment must never be treated as a proxy for talent or effort. It cannot support song-self-tape capture rules in the narrow sense, and it does not directly resolve accompaniment inequality. The evidence is access-only and broad rather than audition specific. citeturn15view1turn15view3turn23view0

### VOICE-S052 evidence note

No exact additional VOICE-S0 B4 source was supplied in this run, so VOICE-S052 was closed as not found rather than being back-filled with an invented source. It therefore supports only a provenance limitation, not any substantive evidence. |

### VOICE-SYN readiness decision

**VOICE-SYN ready with explicit limitations.**

The B4 run resolved the most important previously open blocker: the vocal-health and no-diagnosis boundary is now well supported by a convergent set of high-authority sources, including public voice-care guidance, performing-arts medicine, NHS/ENT clinical information and musician-health guidance. B4 also materially improved fairness handling for access needs, reasonable adjustments, disability, neurodivergence, hearing access, accent bias and gender-diverse voice, and it strengthened the anti-polish logic by showing that devices, data, assistive technology and adaptive equipment are unevenly distributed and therefore must not be conflated with merit. citeturn5view1turn21view0turn8view1turn9view2turn26view0turn12view2turn13view1turn14view1turn15view1

The unresolved issues do **not** block synthesis, but they must be carried explicitly as limitations: detailed belt/mix/registration language remains thin; rich commercial/pop-rock/jazz/folk subtype descriptors remain thin; wider speech-difference evidence is less developed than accent-bias evidence; accompaniment/backing-track inequality is still only partially sourced; body/appearance assumptions remain only indirectly evidenced; and no live Song/Voice report outputs or implementation-side timestamp/stability tests were supplied. These are synthesis and output-spec cautions, not extraction failures. citeturn14view0turn15view1turn23view0

Source-provenance cautions that VOICE-SYN must preserve:
- VOICE-S050 is strong but hiring-context-led rather than singing-audition specific. citeturn14view0turn14view1
- VOICE-S051 is broad digital/equipment access evidence rather than narrow self-tape guidance. citeturn15view1turn15view3
- VOICE-S049 is high-authority but clinical and US-context framed. citeturn13view1
- VOICE-S052 was not supplied and contributes no substantive evidence. |

## Reusable handoff pack for VOICE-SYN

### VOICE-B4 handoff summary

VOICE-B4 used the provisional VOICE-S043–VOICE-S052 pack because no exact S0 B4 ledger was supplied. The strongest outcome is that the branch now has a defensible, high-authority no-diagnosis boundary for singing feedback. Across British Voice Association, BAPAM, NHS/ENT and Musicians’ Union materials, the evidence is consistent: symptoms such as hoarseness, fatigue, discomfort, strain-like sound, reduced range or loss of voice may be described only as cautious observations or reasons to suggest professional support, not as diagnoses or pathology claims. This closes the most serious unresolved safety risk from preflight and B3.

B4 also meaningfully improves fairness coverage. Musicians’ Union, RNID, Drake Music, Johns Hopkins and Accent Bias Britain collectively support non-deficit handling of disability, neurodivergence, hearing difference, assistive technology, communication access, accent bias and gender-diverse voice. Reasonable adjustments are framed as proactive fairness, not exceptional treatment. Deaf and hearing-loss sources support captions, speech-to-text, sign interpretation and hearing technology as legitimate access tools. Drake Music adds strong process evidence that requiring disabled applicants to self-advocate for every adjustment creates extra “disability admin” and can itself be exclusionary. Johns Hopkins adds a clear warning against forcing gendered vocal norms, supporting identity-led and even nonbinary voice outcomes rather than stereotyped expectations.

B4 also strengthens the anti-polish spine established in B3. The batch now has evidence that devices, data, assistive technology, adaptive equipment, room setup and other material supports shape who can participate and how assessable their submission is. This should later help keep audio/technical language separate from sung-vocal merit and should stop expensive setup, specialist equipment or support access becoming proxies for talent.

Compact source-status summary: fully extracted rows were S043, S044, S045, S046, S047, S048 and S049. S050 and S051 are useful but partial, because the former is accent/hiring focused and the latter is broad digital/equipment access evidence rather than narrow song-self-tape guidance. S052 was closed as not found because no exact additional S0 source was supplied. No B4 row remains unresolved.

### Provisional VOICE-B4 findings list

- **VOICE-B4-F01** — B4 sources support a firm no-diagnosis rule for vocal-health language from tape.
- **VOICE-B4-F02** — B4 accessibility sources frame disability, neurodivergence, hearing difference, communication support and gender-diverse voice as access-and-identity matters, not talent deficits.
- **VOICE-B4-F03** — B4 resource-equity evidence strengthens the B3 anti-polish spine by showing that devices, data, assistive technology and adaptive equipment materially affect access and assessability.

### Key vocal-health and safety themes

- Observable strain-like or fatigued sound must remain descriptive, not diagnostic.
- Persistent symptoms belong with GP / ENT / specialist voice-clinic pathways, not with score logic.
- Workload, room acoustics, monitoring and rehearsal conditions affect vocal load and should not be overclaimed from a finished tape.
- Age, adolescence and hormonal context create further caution against over-reading sound.

### Key accessibility, fairness and inclusive voice themes

- Reasonable adjustments are proactive fairness measures.
- Hearing-access tools, captions, STT and assistive listening are legitimate supports.
- Neurodiversity is variation, not deficit.
- Accent prestige is social, not evidence of greater competence.
- Gender-diverse voice handling should be identity-led and non-stereotyped.

### Resource-inequality and anti-polish summary

- Device, data and assistive-tech access are unequal.
- Adaptive equipment and funding routes matter for disabled musicians.
- Home environment and kit quality affect assessability, not talent.
- These findings strengthen rather than replace the B3 assessability-first logic.

### Risk-to-evidence summary for VOICE-PRE-I01–I13

B4 strongly reduces **VOICE-PRE-I03** and materially reduces **VOICE-PRE-I09** and **VOICE-PRE-I10**. It partially reduces **VOICE-PRE-I11** by strengthening the no-stamina-from-tape rule. It contributes only indirectly to **VOICE-PRE-I07** and **VOICE-PRE-I02**, and it does little or nothing to resolve **VOICE-PRE-I01, I04, I05, I06, I08, I12** or **I13**, which therefore remain synthesis, output-spec or live-QA work.

### Baseline preservation notes

Nothing in B4 implies changes to score fields, weights, schema, pipeline, caps, blockers, verdicts, role-fit bounds or the MT acting-plus-song anchor. All accessibility, clinical and inclusive-practice evidence remains guardrail material only and must not be imported as TapeCoach scoring weights or hidden scoring logic.

### Source limitations and deferred issues

- S050 is strong on accent bias, weaker on wider speech-difference evidence.
- S051 is useful on digital and equipment access, but not narrow song-tape process.
- S049 is high-authority but clinical and US-context-led.
- S052 was not supplied.
- Belt/mix/registration and commercial subtype language remain outside B4’s scope.
- Output label/display behaviour, live Song/Voice outputs, score stability and timestamp rendering remain untested.

### VOICE-SYN readiness decision

**VOICE-SYN ready with explicit limitations.**

### Recommended focus for VOICE-SYN

VOICE-SYN should now:
- integrate B1/B2/B3 performance evidence with B4 guardrails;
- make the no-diagnosis rule explicit in sung-vocal wording;
- separate assessability conditions from merit across audio, technical and vocal comments;
- preserve acting/storytelling inside Song without acting-scene leakage;
- explicitly block accent hierarchy, access-deficit language, hearing-difference bias, gendered voice stereotyping and production-polish-as-merit;
- carry unresolved subtype and output-testing limits forward transparently rather than overstating certainty.

### Exact source IDs used

VOICE-S043, VOICE-S044, VOICE-S045, VOICE-S046, VOICE-S047, VOICE-S048, VOICE-S049, VOICE-S050, VOICE-S051, VOICE-S052.

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 4. Branch Scope and Production Context\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 This branch covers 
\f0\b Voice / Singing
\f1\b0  in Song and Musical Theatre contexts. It clarifies sung-vocal evidence, lyric storytelling through song, vocal descriptor specificity, style/subtype caution, accompaniment context, self-tape assessability, vocal-health safety and inclusive voice handling.\
The revised branch outputs are intended to improve:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\ls1\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Song and MT sung-vocal report specificity.\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Song acting/storytelling as lyric/story/communication through song.\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Vocal descriptor precision for pitch, rhythm, tone, diction, phrasing, communication and interpretation.\
\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Safety around no vocal-health diagnosis from tape.\

\ls1\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Output non-regression for Song-only, MT, Acting, Dance and Hybrid contexts.\

\f0\b \cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 VOICE-OS-T01\'96T31
\f1\b0  cover Song-only containment, MT Vocal visibility, Acting/Dance label non-regression, generic praise, poor audio, production polish bias, home-capture fairness, fixed-material advice, no-brief invention, short-cut overclaim, belt/mix overclaim, style overreach, accompaniment fairness, paid-resource bias, vocal-health diagnosis, safe strain-like wording, accent/speech-difference bias, hearing/access support, gender-diverse stereotyping, live-room/process overclaim, timestamp underproduction, next-take specificity, comparison mismatch, rendered timestamp mismatch, Step 2 invention and presentation-padding drift.\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\ls7\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Display checks cover Song/Voice labels, Vocal visibility, component/category wording, comparison-page score/label parity, rendered-versus-persisted timestamps, chronological order, timestamp specificity, next-take specificity and presentation-note discipline.\
\ls7\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Generic-feedback suppression covers phrases such as \'93strong vocal control\'94, \'93lovely tone\'94, \'93secure pitch\'94, \'93powerful belt\'94, \'93nice mix\'94, \'93strong storytelling\'94, \'93perfect song choice\'94, \'93vocal health sounds good\'94, \'93ready because of voice type\'94 and \'93clean audio as vocal merit\'94.\
\ls7\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 No-brief / false-specificity protections block invented song titles, role/world claims, universal cut-length rules, universal era rules and substitute song advice where material is fixed.\
\ls7\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Accessibility and anti-bias protections block access-deficit language, accent hierarchy, gendered voice assumptions, speech-difference deficit inference, body/appearance inference and resource-polish merit.\
\ls7\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Timestamp expectations remain within the current maximum of 8 and must not invent timestamps.\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 15. Compact Branch Handoff Pack\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Voice / Singing is mature at research, rubric, revision, final-audit and output-specificity level and does not require a branch patch before cross-branch consolidation. The branch uses the VOICE prefix and preserves the full traceability set: VOICE-S001\'96VOICE-S052, VOICE-SYN-F01\'96F17, VOICE-AUDIT-I01\'96I20, VOICE-AUDIT-R01\'96R21, VOICE-REV-C01\'96C17, VOICE-REV-S01\'96S18, VOICE-FINAL-D01, VOICE-OS-R rule groups, VOICE-OS-T01\'96T31 and VOICE-OS-I01\'96I12.\
The strongest branch assets are its field-semantics clarification, descriptor spine, safety guardrails and output-specificity test pack. Voice / Singing clarifies that 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  means sung-vocal evidence in Song and Musical Theatre, while Acting / Monologue and Dance retain their non-singing proxy meanings. Song remains vocal-centred but must include interpretive evidence where assessable: lyric intention, communication, phrase action, emotional arc, character or song situation, and acting-through-song. Formal frameworks supplied vocabulary for pitch, rhythm, tone, diction, phrasing, communication and interpretation, but external marks, grades and percentages remain excluded.\
The branch also separates audio/technical assessability from vocal merit, treats accompaniment and self-accompaniment as task/context-specific, blocks production polish and paid-resource access as talent evidence, preserves fixed-material policy, and suppresses generic vocal praise unless anchored to observable evidence. B4 closes the safety gap: no vocal-health diagnosis from tape. Strain-like, fatigued or hoarse sound may be described only as cautious observation. Access needs, disability, neurodivergence, hearing difference, accent, speech difference, gender-diverse voice, assistive technology and reasonable adjustments are non-deficit context.\
Residual limitations are explicit: belt, mix and registration evidence is thin; jazz, folk and broad commercial-pop descriptors are uneven; actor-musician evidence is partial; no Voice-only live outputs exist; frontend labels, comparison-page parity, rendered timestamp parity, score stability, implementation behaviour and rollout effects remain unverified. These do not block consolidation, but they do require later live-output QA and implementation regression before release confidence.\
Verified: source-to-output-spec traceability, revised baseline compatibility, final audit approval and output-specificity mapping. Not verified: live Voice-only reports, frontend category labels, comparison-page behaviour, PDF/export parity, rendered timestamp parity, score stability or production rollout.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 3. Final Audit Scope and Non-Scope\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 This final audit covers whether the revised Voice / Singing baseline correctly implements VOICE-AUDIT recommendations, preserves VOICE-SYN evidence boundaries, avoids overreach, protects the live production architecture and is ready for output-specificity mapping.\
It does not cover live report quality, frontend label rendering, comparison-page parity, persisted-versus-rendered timestamp parity, PDF/export behaviour, score-stability testing, implementation planning or production rollout.\
Deferred to 
\f0\b VOICE-OUTPUT-SPEC
\f1\b0 : display-label tests, timestamp-density tests, generic-feedback adversarial scenarios, comparison-page checks and live-output material requirements.\
Deferred to implementation planning / production rollout: any actual product changes after final approval.\
Preserved without change: six score fields, weights, caps, blockers, verdicts, role-fit bounds, server-side recomputation, Step 1 / Step 2 architecture, locked-field enforcement, deterministic scrubs, material policy and MT acting + song flow.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-FINAL-D01 \'97 Approved with explicit limitations for VOICE-OUTPUT-SPEC / Non-Regression Test Mapping.
\f1\b0 \
Rationale: the revised Voice / Singing baseline implements the evidence-backed, baseline-compatible VOICE-AUDIT recommendations; preserves the VOICE-SYN source boundaries; avoids score-field, weighting, schema, backend, pipeline, cap, verdict, role-fit and recomputation changes; and explicitly carries unresolved areas as limitations rather than hiding them.\
Critical blockers: none.\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 18. Reusable Handoff Pack for VOICE-OUTPUT-SPEC\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-FINAL-AUDIT is complete with explicit limitations. The revised Voice / Singing baseline is approved for Output Specificity / Non-Regression Test Mapping. The final audit verified that VOICE-REV correctly implements the main VOICE-AUDIT recommendations R01\'96R06 and R08\'96R18, preserves R20\'96R21, conditionally limits R07, and appropriately defers R19 to output-specificity / display verification. No blocking VOICE-FINAL-I issues were found.\
The revised baseline preserves the live TapeCoach production architecture: six score fields, Song and MT weights, server-side recomputation, caps, blockers, verdict logic, role-fit bounds, Step 1 / Step 2 pipeline, locked-field enforcement, deterministic scrubs, material-policy guardrails, maximum 3 strengths/improvements, maximum 8 timestamped notes and MT acting + song flow. It does not propose backend, schema, UI, pipeline, weighting or score-field changes.\
The strongest approved changes are: 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  is clarified as sung-vocal evidence in Song / MT; Song remains vocal-centred while requiring interpretive evidence where assessable; acting/storytelling is framed as lyric/storytelling and communication through song rather than acting-scene performance; formal descriptor evidence is converted into observable language for pitch, rhythm, tone, diction, phrasing, communication and interpretation; musical interpretation is made visible through existing fields; audio/technical quality and presentation are separated from vocal merit; accompaniment is task/context-specific; fixed-material policy is protected; generic praise requires evidence anchors; and timestamp / next-take guidance is strengthened within existing limits.\
Safety and fairness handling is approved: no vocal-health diagnosis from tape; strain-like, fatigued or hoarse sound must remain cautious observation only; access needs, disability, neurodivergence, hearing difference, captions, speech-to-text, sign interpretation, assistive technology, accent, speech difference, gender-diverse voice and reasonable adjustments are non-deficit context, not scoring deficits.\
Deferred limitations remain: detailed belt / mix / registration, rich jazz / folk / broad commercial-pop descriptor rubrics, full actor-musician rubric, frontend labels, comparison-page parity, rendered timestamp parity, live Song / Voice QA and score stability. VOICE-OUTPUT-SPEC should convert the revised baseline into rules, adversarial scenarios, non-regression tests and display-layer verification checks.\
Evidence basis: VOICE-S001\'96VOICE-S052; VOICE-SY
\f0\b Check\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 3. Output-Specificity Scope and Non-Scope\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 This mapping covers user-facing output behaviour for Voice / Singing reports: category semantics, report-section specificity, evidence anchors, false-specificity blocks, safety/fairness language, generic-feedback suppression, non-regression tests, adversarial scenarios, display verification requirements and live-output QA package requirements.\
This mapping does not revise the rubric, implement product changes, alter score fields, alter weights, change schemas, change backend or frontend code, run live-output QA, verify rendered labels, verify comparison pages, verify PDF/export parity, or test production score stability.\
Live Song / Voice outputs were not supplied. Therefore, rendered category labels, comparison-page parity, persisted-versus-rendered timestamp parity, PDF/export behaviour, live report quality and score stability remain pending.\
Implementation planning and production rollout remain later stages after the full research/rubric programme and approval. The current live TapeCoach system must remain stable.\
Preserved without change: the six operational score fields, Song and MT weights, server-side recomputation, caps, blockers, verdict logic, role-fit bounds, Step 1 / Step 2 architecture, locked-field enforcement, deterministic scrubs, material-policy guardrails, maximum 3 strengths, maximum 3 improvements, maximum 8 timestamped notes, UK terminology and MT acting + song flow.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0
