Rationale: the approved revised Voice / Singing baseline has been converted into output-specificity rules, user-facing report standards, score-field display semantics, style/subtype rules, tape-observable boundaries, safety/fairness output rules, generic-feedback failure standards, false-specificity standards, preserved non-regression tests, adversarial scenarios, display-layer verification checks and live-output QA requirements.\
Blockers: none for completion of output-spec mapping.\
Can move forward immediately: product-level planning may use the VOICE-OS-R and VOICE-OS-T packs as acceptance criteria for later implementation and regression planning.\
Remaining limitations: live Song / Voice outputs are absent; frontend labels, comparison parity, rendered timestamp parity, score stability, implementation behaviour and production rollout remain unverified.\
Must be tested in live-output QA: category labels, Vocal visibility, Song-only acting/storytelling containment, no-brief invention restraint, generic praise suppression, audio/technical versus vocal merit, timestamp count/order/specificity, next-take specificity, comparison parity and rendered/exported parity.\
Live-output examples are not required before this mapping is complete.\
Recommended mode for the next stage: 
\f0\b standard ChatGPT with file uploads enabled
\f1\b0  for live-output QA when outputs exist; no Deep Research.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 19. Reusable Handoff Pack for Voice / Singing Live-Output QA or Implementation Planning\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-OUTPUT-SPEC is complete with explicit limitations. The approved revised Voice / Singing baseline has been converted into concrete user-facing output rules, non-regression tests, adversarial scenarios, display-layer verification checks and live-output QA requirements. The mapping preserves the current live TapeCoach architecture: six score fields, Song and MT weights, caps, blockers, verdict logic, role-fit bounds, server-side recomputation, Step 1 / Step 2 architecture, locked evidence, deterministic scrubs, maximum 3 strengths/improvements, maximum 8 timestamped notes and the MT acting + song anchor.\
The core output rules establish that 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  means sung-vocal evidence in Song / MT, while Acting and Dance proxy meanings must not receive singing labels. Song-only acting/storytelling must be lyric/story/communication through song, not acting-scene feedback. Song reports must include vocal-plus-interpretive evidence where assessable, using observable descriptors such as pitch, rhythm, tone, diction, phrasing, communication and interpretation. Musical interpretation must appear inside existing fields rather than as a new score. Style/subtype naming is conditional and evidence-led; belt, mix and registration claims are tightly limited because evidence remains thin.\
Safety and fairness rules block vocal-health diagnosis, accent hierarchy, speech-difference deficit inference, gendered voice assumptions, body/appearance or voice-type overclaim, access-deficit language and production polish as merit. Audio, technical setup, accompaniment, backing tracks, self-accompaniment, recording equipment and home setup are assessability/process context, not vocal talent.\
The test pack includes VOICE-OS-T01\'96T31, covering Song-only containment, MT Vocal visibility, Acting/Dance label non-regression, generic praise, poor audio, production polish bias, home-capture fairness, fixed-material advice, no-brief invention, short-cut overclaim, belt/mix overclaim, style overreach, accompaniment fairness, paid-resource bias, vocal-health diagnosis, safe strain-like wording, accent/speech-difference bias, hearing/access support, gender-diverse voice stereotyping, live-room/process overclaim, timestamp underproduction, next-take specificity, comparison mismatch, rendered timestamp mismatch, Step 2 invention and presentation-padding drift.\
Display-layer verification must later check Song/Voice category labels, Vocal visibility, component/category wording, comparison-page score/label parity, rendered-versus-persisted timestamps, chronological order, timestamp specificity, next-take specificity and presentation-note discipline.\
Residual limitations: VOICE-OS-I01\'96I12 cover thin belt/mix/registration evidence, uneven jazz/folk/commercial-pop descriptors, partial actor-musician evidence, absent live Song / Voice outputs, unverified frontend labels, comparison parity, rendered timestamp parity, score stability, no separate musical-interpretation field, no codified score anchors, unverified implementation behaviour and unverified rollout.\
Evidence basis: VOICE-S001\'96VOICE-S052; VOICE-SYN-F01\'96F17; VOICE-AUDIT-I01\'96I20; VOICE-AUDIT-R01\'96R21; VOICE-REV-C01\'96C17; VOICE-REV-S01\'96S18; VOICE-FINAL-D01.\
Verified in this run: output-specificity mapping, non-regression test design, display-check requirements, live-output QA package requirements, preservation and limitation handling.\
Not verified: live Song / Voice output quality, frontend label behaviour, comparison-page behaviour, PDF/export parity, rendered timestamp parity, score stability, implementation behaviour or production rollout.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 3. Revision Scope and Non-Scope\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 This revision covers Voice / Singing baseline wording, evidence requirements, claim-scope rules, safety/fairness guardrails, style/subtype boundaries, generic-feedback suppression, material-policy handling and report-behaviour expectations inside the current six-field TapeCoach architecture.\
This revision does 
\f0\b not
\f1\b0  cover backend implementation, schema changes, score-field changes, weighting changes, cap/blocker/verdict changes, role-fit bound changes, server-side recomputation changes, frontend label implementation, comparison-page rendering, PDF/export behaviour, live-output QA or product rollout.\
Out of scope because of production guardrails: adding a musical-interpretation score field, renaming operational score fields, adding a vocal-health score, adding formal subtype rubrics that require schema changes, importing external exam marks, and changing the MT acting + song flow.\
Pending because no live Song / Voice outputs were supplied: live report quality, rendered category labels, comparison-page parity, timestamp rendering parity, score stability and production-output non-regression.\
Preserve without change: six score fields, Song and MT weights, Step 1 / Step 2 pipeline, locked-field enforcement, deterministic scrubs, maximum 3 strengths, maximum 3 improvements, maximum 8 timestamped notes, material-policy guardrails, safety/accessibility scrubs, server-side recomputation and MT acting + song stability.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-REV is complete with explicit limitations. The revised Voice / Singing baseline strengthens the current Song slice while preserving the live TapeCoach production architecture. It keeps the six operational score fields, Song and MT weights, server-side recomputation, caps, blockers, verdict logic, role-fit bounds, Step 1 / Step 2 architecture, locked evidence, deterministic scrubs, material-policy guardrails and MT acting + song anchor unchanged.\
The core revision clarifies that 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  means sung-vocal evidence in Song / Musical Theatre, while Acting/Monologue and Dance retain their existing proxy meanings and must not receive singing labels. Song remains vocal-centred, but acting/storytelling is now explicitly framed as lyric/storytelling and communication through song, not acting-scene performance. The revised evidence standard requires both vocal technique and interpretive evidence where assessable. Formal descriptor evidence is converted into observable prompt/report guidance for pitch, rhythm, tone, diction, phrasing, communication and interpretation, while external grades, marks and framework weights remain excluded.\
The revision adds song-framed acting-through-song, musical interpretation through existing fields, cautious style/subtype handling, context-specific accompaniment handling, and stronger separation of audio/technical assessability from vocal merit. It blocks production polish, expensive resources, paid accompanist access and studio quality as talent evidence. It preserves fixed-material policy and blocks false specificity such as invented song titles, universal cut lengths, universal era rules, unsupported voice-type fit and alternative material suggestions where material is fixed.\
Safety and fairness revisions add a firm no-diagnosis rule for vocal-health language and non-deficit handling of access needs, disability, neurodivergence, hearing difference, speech difference, accent, gender-diverse voice, reasonable adjustments and assistive technology. Generic vocal praise is now blocked unless anchored to observable evidence. Timestamp and next-take guidance is strengthened within existing caps and locked-evidence limits.\
Compact VOICE-REV-C changes: C01 architecture preservation; C02 sung-vocal semantics; C03 vocal-plus-interpretive standard; C04 descriptor specificity; C05 song-framed acting-through-song; C06 style/subtype limits; C07 assessability/anti-polish; C08 accompaniment context; C09 process-only boundary; C10 no-diagnosis safety; C11 inclusive voice guardrails; C12 material boundaries; C13 generic praise suppression; C14 timestamp/next-take specificity; C15 display deferral; C16 cross-discipline non-regression; C17 Step 2 locked-evidence preservation.\
Revised sections: VOICE-REV-S01\'96S18. Implemented recommendations: R01\'96R06, R08\'96R18. R07 is suppress conditionally / defer. R19 is deferred to output-specificity. R20\'96R21 are preserve-only / guardrail recommendations. Source range used: VOICE-S001\'96VOICE-S052. VOICE-SYN findings used: VOICE-SYN-F01\'96F17. Audit IDs used: VOICE-AUDIT-I01\'96I20 and VOICE-AUDIT-R01\'96R21.\
What was revised: baseline wording, evidence standards, claim-scope rules, style/subtype boundaries, safety/fairness guardrails, generic-feedback suppression and non-regression protections. What was not revised: scoring fields, weights, schema, backend, frontend, pipeline, caps, verdicts, role-fit logic, server-side recomputation or live-output behaviour.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 19. VOICE-REV Decision\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-REV complete with explicit limitations; ready for VOICE-FINAL-AUDIT.
\f1\b0 \
Rationale: the supplied VOICE-SYN and VOICE-AUDIT materials are sufficient to revise the Voice / Singing baseline at rubric/prompt/report-behaviour level without altering production architecture. The revision implements the evidence-backed, baseline-compatible recommendations and preserves all product constraints.\
Critical blockers: none for final audit of the revised baseline.\
Implemented recommendations: VOICE-AUDIT-R01\'96R06 and R08\'96R18.\
Preserve-only recommendations: VOICE-AUDIT-R20 and VOICE-AUDIT-R21.\
Suppressed conditionally / deferred recommendations: VOICE-AUDIT-R07 is limited to cautious evidence-led use; VOICE-AUDIT-R19 is deferred to output-specificity / display verification.\
Limitations to carry forward: thin belt/mix/registration evidence, uneven jazz/folk/commercial-pop descriptors, partial actor-musician evidence, no live Song / Voice outputs, unverified frontend labels, unverified comparison-page parity, unverified rendered timestamp parity and untested score stability.\
Live-output examples are 
\f0\b not required before VOICE-FINAL-AUDIT
\f1\b0  of the revised baseline, but they remain required later for output-specificity / live-output QA.\
Recommended mode for VOICE-FINAL-AUDIT: 
\f0\b standard ChatGPT with file uploads enabled, not Deep Research
\f1\b0 .\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 The baseline and field-semantics problem is clear: 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  must be clarified as sung vocal for Song / MT while preserving Acting and Dance proxy protections.\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 A sufficient public source universe exists for official admissions, formal frameworks, self-tape/audio process and safety/accessibility overlays.\
\ls2\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 The strongest next evidence need is official admissions extraction, because it will establish real audition tasks, style categories, accompaniment rules, acting-through-song expectations and live-vs-recorded boundaries.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 14. Reusable Handoff Pack for VOICE-B1\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-S0 created a verified Voice / Singing source universe with 46 candidate source rows across four batches. The branch should begin with VOICE-B1, focusing on official admissions, schools, conservatoires and MT programmes. The most important baseline reality is that TapeCoach\'92s 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  field is overloaded: sung vocal for Song / Musical Theatre, speech delivery proxy for Acting / Monologue and movement-technique proxy for Dance. Song currently uses 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  as its central sung-vocal score; Musical Theatre uses both acting and vocal as central categories and remains the protected regression anchor. No score-field, weight, schema, backend, pipeline, cap, blocker, verdict or role-fit change is authorised.\
VOICE-B1 should extract real-world audition requirements from sources including ArtsEd, Mountview, Royal Academy of Music, GSA, Royal Welsh, RCS, USC, NYU Tisch, Carnegie Mellon, National Youth Choir, British Youth Music Theatre and related official audition pages. The extraction should prioritise song requirements, style/genre contrast, legit/contemporary/belt/mix/pop-rock language where source-supported, vocal range asks, accompaniment rules, backing-track/live-accompanist handling, song cut lengths, acting-through-song, lyric/storytelling language, self-tape audio/framing rules and live recall/redirection boundaries.\
VOICE-B2 will later extract formal descriptor language from LAMDA, Trinity, ABRSM, LCME and RSL/Rockschool. Those sources may inform observable vocabulary for pitch, time, tone, shape, performance, diction, style, musical communication and character/storytelling, but their marks and grade systems must not become TapeCoach weights. VOICE-B3 should handle professional process and self-tape/audio assessability. VOICE-B4 should handle vocal-health safety, no-diagnosis rules, accessibility and inclusive voice handling.\
Key risks to carry forward are VOICE-PRE-I01\'96VOICE-PRE-I13: technique over story, style not captured, vocal-health diagnosis risk, singing label leakage, acting-scene language leakage, implicit musical interpretation, repertoire overreach, fixed-material policy breach, production/audio polish as vocal merit, accent/diction/speech-difference bias, live-room stamina/direction overclaim, generic vocal praise and timestamp underproduction.\
The next run should be 
\f0\b VOICE-B1 Targeted Batch Extraction
\f1\b0 . It must not browse beyond the assigned B1 source pack once the pack is fixed, must assign final extraction status to every B1 source, and must preserve exact source IDs.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-SYN complete with explicit limitations; ready for VOICE-AUDIT.
\f1\b0 \
Rationale: the completed B1\'96B4 extraction set gives a strong enough evidence base for audit. B1 establishes admissions and programme task realities; B2 supplies the descriptor spine; B3 supplies professional/process and self-tape evidence; B4 closes the key safety and fairness gap around no-diagnosis and access/non-deficit handling.\
There are no critical blockers. No source row remains unresolved. Several rows are partial, duplicate, out of scope, provenance-limited or not found, and those limitations must be preserved in VOICE-AUDIT.\
Live-output examples are not required before VOICE-AUDIT, because the audit will assess baseline/rubric gaps against the source synthesis. Live Song / Voice outputs remain required later for output-specificity/live QA.\
Recommended mode for VOICE-AUDIT: 
\f0\b standard ChatGPT with file uploads enabled
\f1\b0 , not Deep Research. No new public-web extraction is needed unless the audit discovers a material missing handoff.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 18. Reusable Handoff Pack for VOICE-AUDIT\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\fs28 \cf0 VOICE-SYN handoff summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-SYN is complete with explicit limitations and ready for VOICE-AUDIT. The Voice / Singing evidence base now covers VOICE-S001\'96VOICE-S052 across official admissions/programme sources, formal exam frameworks, professional/casting/self-tape process sources, and accessibility/fairness/vocal-health-safety sources. Every source row is closed with a final status or explicit limitation; no source row remains unresolved.\
The strongest synthesis result is that Song is not technique-only display. Across admissions, formal frameworks and professional sources, sung work is consistently both vocal and interpretive: pitch, rhythm, tone, diction, phrasing and technical control sit alongside lyric intention, communication, character, story, style and acting-through-song. This supports clarifying 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  as sung-vocal evidence in Song and Musical Theatre while keeping acting/storytelling visible as a supporting category and avoiding acting-scene leakage.\
The formal descriptor spine is now strong: pitch/intonation, rhythm/time, tone, diction/intelligibility, phrasing/shape, communication and interpretation are well supported. Style evidence is useful but uneven. Classical/legit, contemporary MT, classical art song, unaccompanied and accompanied/backing-track contexts are stronger; belt, mix, jazz, folk and broad commercial/pop descriptors remain thinner and must be carried as limitations.\
B1\'96B3 strongly support assessability-first self-tape handling: clear audio, balanced accompaniment, readable framing, simple capture and workable room acoustics are conditions for fair assessment, not vocal merit. B4 strengthens this with resource-equity evidence: devices, data, assistive technology, adaptive equipment and home environment affect participation and assessability, not talent.\
B4 also closes the major safety risk: vocal-health language must be no-diagnosis and observation-only. Strain-like sound, fatigue, hoarseness or reduced range may be described cautiously but never diagnosed or treated as pathology. Accessibility evidence supports non-deficit handling of disability, neurodivergence, hearing difference, communication support, accent, gender-diverse voice and reasonable adjustments.\
Live-output behaviour remains untested: Song/Voice labels, timestamp rendering, score stability and report specificity must be handled later in output-spec/live QA.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Source-family evidence summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 B1 admissions sources strongly support song contrast, task-aware repertoire, acting-through-song, accompaniment differences, self-tape assessability and live-room boundaries. B2 formal frameworks strongly support descriptor language but must not supply TapeCoach weights. B3 professional/casting/self-tape sources strongly support assessability versus polish, lyric/storytelling, accompaniment handling and process-only callbacks. B4 safety/access sources strongly support no-diagnosis, non-deficit access handling, accent fairness, hearing access, gender-diverse voice caution and resource-equity guardrails.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Style/subtype evidence summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Strongest: classical/legit, contemporary MT, classical art song/opera-adjacent, unaccompanied singing, accompanied/backing-track song, audition cuts, MT song in multi-component tape. Medium: actor-musician, self-accompanied song, commercial/pop vocal. Thin: belt, mix, detailed registration, jazz, folk and broader commercial-pop descriptors.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Tape-observable versus process-only summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Finished song tape can usually support pitch, timing, diction, phrasing, tone, lyric intention, acting-through-song, visible communication, accompaniment balance and basic assessability if audio/video conditions allow. It cannot safely prove response to direction, learning speed, sight-singing, aural skills, callback readiness, training potential, stamina, health status, access need, identity, or professional readiness beyond observable task compliance and assessability.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Safety/accessibility/fairness summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Use no-diagnosis language. Treat strain-like or fatigued sound as cautious observation only. Do not infer pathology, respiratory condition, convalescence, psychological state or medical status. Treat hearing access, captions, STT, sign interpretation, assistive tech, reasonable adjustments, disability, neurodivergence, accent, speech difference and gender-diverse voice as access/fairness context, not performance deficits.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Generic-feedback risk summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 High-risk generic phrases include \'93strong vocal control\'94, \'93lovely tone\'94, \'93good breath support\'94, \'93secure pitch\'94, \'93emotional connection\'94, \'93powerful belt\'94, \'93nice mix\'94, \'93good legit quality\'94, \'93expressive singing\'94, \'93great musicality\'94, \'93strong storytelling\'94, \'93professional song choice\'94, \'93perfect song choice\'94, \'93vocal health sounds good\'94, \'93ready because of voice type\'94, \'93strong presence\'94 and \'93clean audio as vocal merit\'94. These require observable anchors or must be blocked.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Preliminary risk-resolution summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-PRE-I03 is resolved as a safety boundary. VOICE-PRE-I09 and VOICE-PRE-I11 are strongly reduced. VOICE-PRE-I01, I02, I05, I06, I07, I08, I10 and I12 are partially resolved and must be audited. VOICE-PRE-I04 and I13 remain largely output/display/live-QA risks.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Limitation register summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Carry forward: thin belt/mix/registration detail; uneven pop-rock/jazz/folk/commercial descriptors; partial actor-musician evidence; B3 singer-specific process partly opera/generic shaped; S034 snippet limitation; S037 opinion/paywall limitation; S041 opera/remote-context limitation; S050 accent/hiring focus; S051 broad digital/equipment access; S052 not found; live outputs absent; display labels unverified; timestamp rendering and score stability untested; no codified score anchor tables; no separate musical-interpretation field.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Audit priority preview\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-AUDIT should prioritise: vocal technique versus story balance; sung-vocal field semantics; style/subtype specificity; song-only acting/storytelling without acting-scene leakage; musical interpretation inside existing fields; assessability versus polish; audio/technical versus vocal merit; no-diagnosis vocal-health boundary; accessibility/inclusive voice protections; accent/diction fairness; gender-diverse voice caution; repertoire/fixed-material boundary; live-room overclaim; generic praise; timestamp density; MT non-regression; Acting and Dance label non-regression.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Baseline preservation notes\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 No finding implies a score-field, weighting, cap, blocker, verdict, role-fit, schema, backend, pipeline or server-side recomputation change. The current live production architecture remains preserved. MT acting + song remains the protected regression anchor.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Exact source ID range used\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-S001\'96VOICE-S052, with shorthand S### normalised to VOICE-S###.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 What was and was not synthesised\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Synthesised: B1\'96B4 source evidence, source-family boundaries, descriptor spine, safety/fairness evidence, claim-scope limits, baseline compatibility and audit priorities.\
Not synthesised as verified product behaviour: live Song / Voice report outputs, frontend label behaviour, comparison-page behaviour, rendered timestamp parity, score stability, implementation behaviour or production rollout effects.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 19. Completion Statement\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 11. Voice / Singing Live-Output QA Status\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 True Voice / Singing live outputs are not available in the supplied materials. The user explicitly states that there are no voice-only outputs currently available and that Voice / Singing is a new feature being prepared for production release. MT acting+song PDFs and comparison/result examples were supplied, but they are bridge/current-output examples rather than revised Voice-only QA.\
Voice / Singing live QA has therefore not been completed. Untested areas include live Song / Voice report quality, frontend category labels, comparison-page parity, PDF/export behaviour, rendered timestamp parity, persisted-versus-rendered timestamp parity, score stability, and behaviour after implementation/rollout.\
Live materials required later include at minimum: Song-only report with brief, Song-only report with no brief, poor-audio/track-balance Song report, simple home-capture Song report, polished-production Song report, MT acting+song report, rendered category-label screenshot, comparison-page screenshot/export, timestamped-notes section, next-take plan, presentation/professional standards section, JSON/report object snippet, PDF/export if available, access/adapted-context output if available, and repeated same-video outputs for score stability.\
Absence of live outputs does not block research maturity. It does block product release sign-off for implemented revised Voice / Singing behaviour.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 12. Voice / Singing Patch Decision\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\fs24 \cf0 No Voice / Singing patch required; branch is mature enough for implementation planning with limitations.
\f1\b0 \
Rationale: Voice / Singing meets the lean v5 standard at research/rubric/output-specificity level. It has preflight, source census, targeted extraction batches, synthesis, audit, revision, final audit and output-specificity mapping. It preserves the live TapeCoach architecture, clarifies the overloaded 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  field for Song / MT, protects Acting and Dance label containment, provides an observable descriptor spine, separates interpretation from acting-scene leakage, establishes no-diagnosis vocal-health rules, codifies access-safe inclusive voice handling, and creates output-specificity tests and live-QA requirements. Residual weaknesses are correctly carried as limitations rather than hidden or over-implemented.\
Critical blockers: none for implementation planning preparation.\
Patch scope if needed: none. The remaining work is live-output QA after implementation or current-output bridge checks where relevant, not a VOICE-PATCH.\
What should not be reopened: VOICE-S0 source census, B1\'96B4 extraction, VOICE-SYN, VOICE-AUDIT, VOICE-REV, VOICE-FINAL-AUDIT, or VOICE-OUTPUT-SPEC.\
Deep Research required: no.\
Standard ChatGPT sufficient: yes, for any future implementation-readiness handoff consolidation or live-QA prompt creation.\
Live outputs required for patch: no, because no patch is recommended.\
Can proceed before implementation planning: yes, with explicit limitations carried into implementation planning and later live-output QA.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 14. Reusable Handoff Pack\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 VOICE-V5-MATURITY-AUDIT reviewed the completed Voice / Singing branch against the newer lean v5 branch-development standard. The maturity decision is that no Voice / Singing patch is required. The branch is mature enough for future implementation planning with explicit limitations and later live-output QA.\
The strongest Voice / Singing assets are its full traceability spine and mature safety/fairness boundaries. The branch preserves VOICE-S001\'96VOICE-S052, VOICE-SYN-F01\'96F17, VOICE-AUDIT-I01\'96I20, VOICE-AUDIT-R01\'96R21, VOICE-REV-C01\'96C17, VOICE-REV-S01\'96S18, VOICE-FINAL-D01, VOICE-OS-R onward, VOICE-OS-T01\'96T31 and VOICE-OS-I01\'96I12. It clarifies 
\f2\fs26 vocal
\f1\fs24  as sung-vocal evidence in Song / Musical Theatre while preserving Acting speech-delivery and Dance no-singing containment. It keeps Song vocal-centred but requires interpretive evidence where assessable: lyric intention, communication, phrase action, story and acting-through-song. It converts formal frameworks into observable descriptor language for pitch, rhythm, tone, diction, phrasing, communication and interpretation without importing marks, grades or weights.\
The branch also strongly separates audio/technical assessability from vocal merit, treats accompaniment/backing/self-accompaniment as context-specific, blocks production polish and paid-resource access as talent evidence, and protects fixed-material policy. Safety and fairness coverage is mature: no vocal-health diagnosis from tape; strain-like, fatigued or hoarse sound remains observation-only; access needs, disability, neurodivergence, hearing difference, accent, speech difference, gender-diverse voice and assistive technology are non-deficit context.\
Limitations remain but are correctly carried forward: detailed belt/mix/registration evidence is thin; jazz/folk/broad commercial-pop descriptors are uneven; full actor-musician evidence is partial; neurodivergence operational detail is broad; no true Voice-only live outputs exist; frontend labels, comparison-page parity, rendered timestamp parity, score stability, implementation behaviour and rollout effects remain unverified.\
The branch does not need a focused patch. Later work should be implementation planning plus live-output QA when Voice / Singing outputs exist. Live-output QA is not required to prove research maturity, but it is required before release confidence for implemented revised behaviour.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0
